Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis

Details:
The failing test `testParentOptionAndChildOption` expects that when parsing the command line `--parent error --child exception`, a maximum restriction on the parent option is violated, thus throwing an OptionException.

The current bug report explains that minimum and maximum constraints on a group do not consider child groups or options correctly because groups are not added to the CommandLine. Specifically, the method WriteableCommandLine.addOption(Option) is responsible for adding options to the command line. However, upon inspecting WriteableCommandLineImpl.addOption(Option), the method currently only adds the option itself into internal collections but does not traverse or add parent or child group options to the command line.

Moreover, the method WriteableCommandLineImpl.hasOption(Option) merely checks whether the options collection directly contains the option, which returns false for groups if they are not added explicitly.

The GroupImpl class has minimum and maximum constraints via getMinimum() and getMaximum(), but because groups are never added to the command line, their constraints are not enforced properly when determining if options exist. The test expects a maximum restriction violation on the parent group, but since the group is missing from the command line and only direct options are counted, this constraint is not correctly checked.

Hence, the root cause of the bug is that the presence of child options or child groups does not trigger adding the parent group option to the command line in WriteableCommandLineImpl.addOption. Consequently, the maximum and minimum constraints on the groups are not respected during option validation, causing test failures like in testParentOptionAndChildOption.

The reported fix suggests modifying WriteableCommandLineImpl.addOption(Option) to add the parent groups when a child option is added, ensuring that group constraints are enforced correctly. This fits the test's failure symptom and the bug report's description perfectly.

No direct relevance from recent bug reports was found, so the diagnosis relies primarily on the code inspection and the current bug description.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
